newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's PIA sees growth in Far East.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's PIA sees growth in Far East.

text.p: The state-run Pakistan International Airline (PIA) said on Wednesday it had good prospects for growth in the Far East.

"East of Pakistan is the growth area in the future for the PIA," PIA Chairman Shahid Khaqan Abbasi told reporters, saying the airline was planning to increase frequency to Japan and other destinations in the Far East.

Abbasi said PIA was considering selling its hotels in the United States and France to raise money to buy new planes that would replace its ageing aircraft, including Boeing 747-200 and Fokker F-27-200/400.
PIA's hotel in New York can raise more than $200 million which can partly finance the new aircraft, he said.
"The airline needs wide-bodied and long-range aircraft for future needs," he said, adding: "We are evaluating several options."
The replacement, to cost $600 to $900 million, is likely to be completed in 12 to 15 months, he said. "We will take the final decision in the next two months."
PIA can provide between 20 and 30 percent equity needed for the new aircraft and the rest will be paid by raising money from financial institutions, he said.

He said PIA was considering Boeing 777, MD-11 and Airbus A340 as possible replacements. For the replacement of smaller aircraft, PIA was looking at aircraft produced in Canada, France, Sweden, Brazil and Indonesia.
PIA now has eight Boeing 747-200s, nine Airbus A300-B4s, six Airbus A310-300s, six Boeing 737-300s, two Boeing 707 cargo planes, 13 Fokker F-27s and two Twin Otters.
Abbasi said PIA's privatisation programme was at a low priority. "We have to improve its profitability first."

PIA's after-tax profit plunged to 65 million rupees in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) from 293 million in the year-ago period. In the first half of fiscal 1996/97 to December, its profit dipped to 22 million compared to 182 million in the year-ago period.
Its 10-rupee share closed unchanged at 10.60 at the Karachi Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
